page: Google Cloud Platform n2d-standard-16 is a general-purpose virtual machine featuring 16 dedicated vCPUs and 64.0 GB of system memory, yielding a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. The instance is powered by an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor built on the x86_64 architecture, consisting of 8 physical cores with 2 threads per core. The CPU cache configuration includes 32 KB of L1d cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. This server does not include local storage or integrated GPU hardware, and it offers zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

In benchmark evaluations, the n2d-standard-16 demonstrates strong single-core CPU performance, with stress-ng single-core tests placing it in the top 25% of tested instances. Multi-core performance, including stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core metrics, falls within the average range. Memory bandwidth benchmarks, such as read-only large block and write large block tests, also register average tier results. For language model tasks, the instance achieves strong text generation speeds of 277.2 tokens per second with a small 135M model, though prompt processing and medium 7B model inference speeds remain in the average tier.

The qualitative cost profile of the n2d-standard-16 reflects a standard resource density suitable for general-purpose workloads. The absence of local NVMe storage represents a tradeoff, requiring network-attached storage for persistent data. This configuration is suited for workloads such as static web serving, database operations, software compilation, and moderate text processing tasks that benefit from dedicated AMD EPYC compute resources without requiring specialized GPU acceleration.
